findings.evidence: "The benefits team tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Name the specific document staff can request (e.g., "a printed copy of the current budget summary").
findings.violation: "A printed copy" has no clear antecedent - it's unclear whether this refers to the budget, the catalog, or some other document, since no specific document was named.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: State explicitly which clock resumes (e.g., "the 90-day service requirement resumes counting").
findings.violation: "The stipend clock" is never defined - it's unclear whether this refers to the 90-day service requirement or the per-benefit-year claim cycle.

findings.evidence: "In addition, eligibility for the workspace stipend depends on several details the reviewer checks one at a time."
findings.fix: Use one consistent name for the stipend throughout, or explicitly state that "workspace stipend" and "home-office equipment stipend" are the same program.
findings.violation: The document is titled "Home-Office Equipment Stipend Policy" and refers elsewhere to "the stipend," but this paragraph introduces a separate-sounding "workspace stipend" without clarifying whether it's the same program or a different one.

findings.evidence: "Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order before the review begins."
findings.fix: Clarify what "the review" refers to, or reorder the process so approval is obtained before the approval form is required as an input.
findings.violation: This is circular - the "manager's approval form" cannot be submitted before "the review" if the review is what produces the manager's approval.

findings.evidence: "The summary shows the equipment cost and the requested delivery date."
findings.fix: Clarify whether employees purchase equipment before or after approval, and remove whichever field doesn't match that model.
findings.location: How to Apply, confirmation summary sentence
findings.violation: A "requested delivery date" implies the equipment hasn't been purchased or delivered yet, but the same section already requires submitting "the receipt" (proof of a completed purchase) before this step - the two imply contradictory purchase states.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: Reconcile the two sections so the documentation requirements are stated once, consistently.
findings.violation: This contradicts How to Apply, which requires "the receipt" and "the original purchase order" as mandatory upfront submissions, with no mention that a photo suffices or that some requests need more.

findings.evidence: "this office may ask for a brief photo check once a year"
findings.fix: Name the specific office (e.g., "the benefits team may ask for...").
findings.violation: "This office" has no antecedent in this section - no office was named immediately before this sentence, so the reader can't tell which team performs the check.

findings.evidence: "the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device"
findings.fix: Split into separate sentences, state the one-device rule and the second-device exception clearly, and reconcile with the "one claim per benefit year" limit stated in Eligibility.
findings.violation: The sentence simultaneously asserts a one-device-per-category limit and describes an approved second device, which is self-contradictory; it also conflicts with Eligibility's "one claim per employee per benefit year." The sentence is also a 90+ word run-on that is very hard to parse.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person for consistency, and either add actual term definitions or rename the heading to match its content.
findings.violation: This section shifts to second-person voice ("you") while the rest of the document uses third person ("employees," "the applicant"), and despite the heading "Terminology Notes," it defines no terms - it just restates process steps.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Align this section's steps with How to Apply, or remove the redundant section.
findings.violation: This process description omits the manager's approval form and purchase order required in How to Apply, and reorders steps (starting with "confirming eligibility") inconsistently with the earlier section.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicated paragraph and either delete this section or replace it with actual special-case guidance, keeping a single consistent owner for budget review.
findings.violation: This is a near-verbatim duplicate of the Program Overview paragraph but attributes the same task to a different party ("finance liaison" vs. "the benefits team"), directly contradicting it; the heading "Special Cases" also doesn't match content that describes no actual special case.

findings.evidence: "Once approved, the team schedules the reimbursement for the next pay cycle."
findings.fix: Clarify the handoff between the benefits team and finance office in the reimbursement approval process.
findings.violation: This conflicts with Reimbursement Amounts, which states "The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount" - it's unclear whether the benefits team or the finance office has final authority over approving/scheduling payment.

findings.evidence: "The determination of stipend eligibility happens before any payment goes out. The escalation of repeat requests happens automatically within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Rewrite to name the responsible party (e.g., "The benefits team determines eligibility...") and define what qualifies as a "repeat request."
findings.violation: Both sentences use nominalized, passive phrasing that hides who performs the action, and "repeat requests" is never defined anywhere else in the document.

findings.evidence: "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicated/contradictory text and replace this section with actual guidance on how to ask questions or find updates, or rename the heading.
findings.violation: This duplicates the "date stamp" sentence from Program Overview but reattributes it from the equipment catalog (updated quarterly) to the stipend budget (tracked at fiscal year start), creating a contradiction about what people operations actually maintains; the heading "Questions and Updates" also doesn't match content that has no Q&A or contact information.
